name: Secular humanism
summary: Secular humanism holds that ethics and knowledge rest on human reason, evidence and experience rather than on divine authority, and that society should be organised around free inquiry, human rights and democracy. Politically it demands strict separation of church and state, civil liberties and secular education, and in the Humanist Manifesto II tradition it also supports reproductive and sexual freedom, equality, social provision for basic needs, and international cooperation.
scope: The organised secular humanist movement as defined by the American Humanist Association's Humanist Manifesto II (1973), Paul Kurtz's A Secular Humanist Declaration (1980) and the general scholarly account of the movement. It excludes religious humanism and Renaissance humanism, and because the movement prescribes no economic programme, most economic and foreign-policy answers are low-confidence inferences.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Manifesto II calls for social provision of basic needs such as health care, though it names no single delivery system.

public-ownership.rationale: Manifesto II names no preferred economic system and humanists range from libertarian to socialist, so ownership is left open.

cut-welfare.rationale: Manifesto II backs social provision of basic needs and a guaranteed minimum income, so cutting welfare runs against its stated economic ethic.

worker-ownership.rationale: Manifesto II wants workplace democracy but does not endorse collective ownership; adherents are split between market and socialist views.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Manifesto II lists protection from invasions of privacy among civil liberties, which counts against surveillance justified by security.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Neither Manifesto II nor the secondary sources address drugs; adherents' libertarian and paternalist strains split.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Secular humanists give priority to free inquiry and free speech (the Declaration's first plank), so most resist legal speech limits.

strong-leader.rationale: Humanism is defined by commitment to freedom and democracy and opposes totalitarianism, so bypassing legislatures is rejected.

state-harmful.rationale: Manifesto II relies on political democracy, fair courts and social provision, which presuppose a legitimate state.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Manifesto II holds consenting adults free of legal sanction in their sexual lifestyles but rejects exploitation; commercial sex is not mentioned.

decide-locally.rationale: Manifesto II wants decentralised participatory decision-making yet also a world community with transnational governance, so it pulls both ways.

traditional-family.rationale: Manifesto II rejects repressive attitudes on sex and family, defending divorce, birth control and varied lifestyles, rather than one traditional model.

abortion-legal.rationale: Manifesto II explicitly affirms the right to abortion alongside birth control and divorce.

more-religion-public.rationale: The Declaration and Manifesto II call for strict separation of church and state and reject supernaturalism as a basis for public decisions.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Manifesto II opposes division along national lines though allowing pride in national origins; preservation as a priority is not its concern.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Manifesto II calls for a world community with transnational federal government and strengthening of international bodies.

nation-first.rationale: Manifesto II rejects division along national lines and puts the world community ahead of national sovereignty.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Humanists value human rights but Manifesto II hopes war will be obsolete and disputes settled peacefully; adherents split.

limit-growth.rationale: Manifesto II urges conservation and an end to waste but also champions technology and the end of poverty; no stance on growth limits.

central-planning.rationale: Manifesto II is wary of both capitalist and communist dogma and humanists oppose Marxist-Leninist rule.

basic-income.rationale: Manifesto II endorses a minimum guaranteed income where resources permit.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Manifesto II wants an economy judged by human benefit but no industrial policy is described.

one-party-rule.rationale: Humanism is defined by commitment to freedom and democracy, and Manifesto II demands legal opposition and rejects state-imposed ideology.

democracy-best.rationale: Kurtz and colleagues call commitment to freedom and democracy the defining characteristic of humanism, and Manifesto II calls for political democracy.

direct-votes.rationale: Manifesto II supports participatory democracy but names no mechanism such as referendums.

workers-councils.rationale: Manifesto II extends participation to workplaces but keeps parliamentary political democracy with legal opposition.

natural-rulers.rationale: Manifesto II opposes discrimination and supports equal opportunity and democracy, which exclude innate rulers.

political-violence-never.rationale: Manifesto II hopes war becomes obsolete and favours peaceful settlement, but no absolute ban on political violence is stated.

war-builds-character.rationale: Manifesto II calls war obsolete and urges peaceful settlement of disputes and cuts in military spending.

separate-church-state.rationale: The Declaration's second plank and Manifesto II demand strict separation of religion from the state and no public money favouring religious bodies.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Humanists reject dogma and supernaturalism as a basis for decisions and ethics, and demand a secular state.

military-superiority.rationale: Manifesto II urges reducing military spending and war's end, not pursuit of superiority.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Manifesto II opposes discrimination based on race, religion or national origin and favours a world community.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Humanists reject Marxist-Leninist doctrine and Manifesto II criticises communist dogma.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Manifesto II supports equal opportunity, aid to the disadvantaged and a minimum income, but not strict equal outcomes.

civilizational-union.rationale: Manifesto II rejects divisions along national lines in favour of a universal world community, not religious blocs.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Humanist ethics is grounded in human need, compassion and shared welfare rather than egoism, though it values individual fulfilment.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Humanism puts individual human rights and freedom at the centre of its politics.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Manifesto II urges conservation yet humanism stresses human welfare and does not stand above nature; intrinsic value is contested.

limit-population.rationale: Manifesto II calls for international cooperation to check excessive population growth, including aid for birth control.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Manifesto II treats technology as vital to progress and humanism is optimistic about science.

restore-past-order.rationale: Humanism rejects inherited dogma and holds that morality and society are improved by reason and experience.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Manifesto II judges economic systems and technology by their consequences for well-being, and humanism favours testing beliefs by evidence.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Humanism's faith in science and technology for human betterment excludes a foraging ideal.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Manifesto II supports social provision of basic needs yet does not call for distribution by need across the economy.

production-for-use.rationale: Manifesto II criticises capitalist dogma but does not demand abolition of profit production.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Not a humanist doctrine; Manifesto II is critical of capitalism's dogma but also of communism's.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Humanists oppose totalitarian and Marxist-Leninist rule, and Manifesto II requires legal opposition and civil liberties.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Manifesto II is critical of capitalist dogma but attributes war to nationalism and division, not capitalism alone.

taxation-theft.rationale: Manifesto II supports public provision, which depends on taxes.

harm-principle.rationale: Manifesto II holds consenting adults free from legal sanction in private conduct while rejecting exploitation.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Humanism centres individual rights but Manifesto II also affirms equal treatment for groups defined by race and sex; contested.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Humanism treats democratic participation as defining, so exit is no substitute for voting.

positive-liberty.rationale: Manifesto II ties freedom to social provision, equal opportunity and a guaranteed minimum income, pointing to material conditions of freedom.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Manifesto II opposes racism and discrimination by race, and humanism rests on equal worth.

organic-representation.rationale: Manifesto II's democratic model relies on free parties, political opposition and elections.

total-state.rationale: Manifesto II demands civil liberties, legal opposition and separation of ideology from the state; Haworth sees humanism as opposed to totalitarianism.

national-rebirth.rationale: Humanism opposes nationalism and fascism, per Haworth, and Manifesto II rejects national division.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Manifesto II calls war obsolete and rejects national divisions.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Humanism relies on reason, evidence and the scientific method as means of reaching truth, not on power-determined truth.

universal-morality.rationale: Secular humanists reject absolutist systems, yet hold that objective ethical standards can emerge through deliberation; adherents split between universal and relativist readings.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not a humanist doctrine and Manifesto II opposes national division; adherents differ.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Manifesto II extends participatory democracy to the economy, workplaces, schools and families.

economic-freedom.rationale: Manifesto II treats political democracy as basic but is critical of purely capitalist dogma; no link to economic freedom is asserted.

rule-by-example.rationale: Humanism favours law, rights and democracy over rule by moral example.

national-self-determination.rationale: Manifesto II is internationalist and opposes national division yet backs democracy; split.

force-without-un.rationale: Manifesto II favours transnational governance and peaceful settlement, so unilateral force is disfavoured.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Secular humanism treats reason and the scientific method as the proper basis for knowledge and rejects faith and dogma as authority.

dominated-front.rationale: Manifesto II's world-community outlook disfavours bloc confrontation.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Manifesto II seeks to eliminate discrimination on the basis of sex and supports equal opportunity.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Manifesto II seeks to eliminate racial discrimination and humanism opposes racism.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Humanist values of multiculturalism and toleration per later humanist ethics oppose forced assimilation.

elite-replacement.rationale: The claim is a conspiracy theory, at odds with humanist reliance on evidence and opposition to discrimination by national origin.

national-mission.rationale: Manifesto II opposes national division and ideological state missions.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Manifesto II stresses human rights, reproductive freedom and consent in birth control; coerced eugenics conflicts with this.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Manifesto II supports social provision, a guaranteed minimum income and public education, far beyond a minimal state.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Manifesto II seeks to eliminate discrimination by race, religion, sex, age or national origin; humanist principles include justice, fairness and equality.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Manifesto II insists on religious liberty and free inquiry, so legal limits on conversion are rejected.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A religion-based ban conflicts with the demand that law not rest on religious doctrine.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Manifesto II rejects public support for religious bodies and the Declaration's separation plank covers state schooling.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Manifesto II demands political democracy, fair courts and free opposition, which embody consent.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Humanists hope for peaceful settlement but ethics is consequence-based, not an absolute non-aggression axiom.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Manifesto II stresses cooperation and an international community; Darwinist struggle is not endorsed.

vanguard-party.rationale: Humanists oppose Marxist-Leninist and totalitarian rule, and Manifesto II demands free opposition parties.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Manifesto II commits to eliminating poverty, aiding the disadvantaged and basic social provision.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Manifesto II ties population control to development but does not call it the main cause of poverty.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Later humanist ethics supports multiculturalism and toleration, per sources.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Manifesto II demands civil liberties and fair courts, with no emergency exceptions mentioned.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Neither the manifestos nor the scholarship discuss price controls, and adherents range from market-friendly to interventionist.

party-controls-media.rationale: Manifesto II demands free speech and press and the Declaration makes free inquiry its first principle.

party-commands-army.rationale: Manifesto II separates ideology from the state and opposes party-state totalitarianism.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Pay for legislators never comes up in humanist texts, so there is no movement position.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Manifesto II calls for transnational federal government and a world community above national sovereignty.

clerical-rule.rationale: Humanists reject supernaturalism as basis for decisions and demand strict separation of religion from the state.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Manifesto II calls for free expression and opposes repressive attitudes.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Humanists value toleration and multiculturalism but also criticise cultural practices that violate human rights; split.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Manifesto II calls for moral and sex education, responsibility and equality in schools.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The Declaration lists evolution as a plank and humanists accept methodological naturalism in science teaching.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Manifesto II opposes repressive attitudes on sexuality and calls for free expression, while rejecting exploitation.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Humanists defend religious liberty but also strict equal treatment under law; split.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Manifesto II rejects repressive social attitudes and favours individual freedom in life choices.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Manifesto II demands civil liberties and political democracy; commitment to freedom is humanism's defining characteristic.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Manifesto II calls for aid to developing regions and international cooperation to end poverty.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Manifesto II opposes nuclear weapons and urges disarmament.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Humanist texts name no preferred way to choose a head of state, so the movement is indifferent.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Monetary institutions are outside what the manifestos or Declaration address; no humanist position exists.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A Marxist debate; humanists simply condemn Soviet suppression of rights.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Manifesto II urges conservation, yet humanists insist on evidence; split.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Humanists want separation, not state control of religion; Kurtz opposed state atheism.

character-from-environment.rationale: Humanists draw on science and neither side of nature versus nurture is a doctrine.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Manifesto II requires fair courts, legal opposition and civil liberties against arbitrary power.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical mixed-constitution theory is not part of humanist political writing, which simply endorses democracy.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Marxist doctrine not held; humanists oppose Marxist-Leninist rule.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Manifesto II rejects national division and discrimination by national origin and hopes war will be obsolete.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Manifesto II demands religious liberty and free inquiry; humanists reject religious punishments.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Manifesto II rejects divisions along ethnic and national lines.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: A Marxist thesis; humanists stress reason and ideas but also material progress.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Manifesto II demands fair courts and protection of civil liberties against majorities.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Humanists oppose violent revolution and Marxist-Leninist methods.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Manifesto II seeks equal opportunity and elimination of discrimination by birth categories.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Manifesto II affirms equality across nations and opposes discrimination by national origin.

patriotic-education.rationale: Manifesto II allows pride in national origins but opposes divisions along national lines.

delink-world-market.rationale: Manifesto II backs international cooperation and aid to developing regions.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Manifesto II seeks to eliminate discrimination and supports equal opportunity.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Manifesto II emphasises civil liberties, fair courts and human rights as protections.

elective-rulers.rationale: Manifesto II calls for political democracy.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Humanist ethics rests on welfare and empathy; Manifesto II is silent on animals.

animal-use-humane.rationale: The manifestos do not discuss animal use; humanists hold mixed views on food and research.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Hierarchical duty differs from humanist egalitarianism but charity is valued; split.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Humanism emphasises active participation in democracy and social improvement.

native-born-offices.rationale: Manifesto II opposes discrimination by national origin.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Manifesto II supports aid for developing regions.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Manifesto II holds war obsolete and opposes national divisions.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Haworth describes humanism as opposed to fascist and Marxist-Leninist totalitarianism alike.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Historical claim contrary to mainstream scholarship; humanists follow evidence.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Humanist texts stress equality and protection from exploitation but never compare male and female victimisation.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Humanists hold democracy and human rights as universal.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Manifesto II seeks demilitarisation and democratic civil control.

paid-care-work.rationale: Manifesto II seeks sex equality but does not mention paying for domestic labour, so the movement is silent.

filial-duty.rationale: Humanist ethics does not set out family duties of this kind and adherents differ on them.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Manifesto II holds that divorce should be legal and rejects repressive attitudes toward family life.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Binding mandates and instant recall are council-democracy ideas; humanist texts back democracy without this mechanism.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The manifestos oppose discrimination but do not say whether unequal outcomes alone count as proof of it.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Manifesto II criticises waste, but the movement has no doctrine on consumption and many adherents are comfortable with it.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Manifesto II calls for peaceful settlement and cuts in military spending.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Manifesto II opposes war and domination between nations.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Manifesto II seeks to check population growth.

job-guarantee.rationale: Manifesto II supports minimum income, not a job guarantee.

non-intervention.rationale: Manifesto II favours transnational governance and human rights.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is an internal labour matter that humanist sources do not touch.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Manifesto II treats divorce and varied lifestyles as legitimate but not abolition of legal marriage.

local-production.rationale: Localism in production is not a humanist theme, which stresses world community and technology.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Manifesto II backs a world community and transnational governance.

religious-nation.rationale: Humanists demand strict church-state separation and oppose discrimination by religion.

defeat-communism.rationale: Humanists criticise Soviet atheism and communist dogma but prefer peaceful coexistence; split.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Manifesto II wants basic needs met but does not choose between public and private delivery.

religion-illusion.rationale: Humanists reject supernaturalism but do not tie its fading to material conditions; Marxist thesis.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Humanist sources do not give a historical verdict on capitalism, and Manifesto II criticises its dogma while crediting technology.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Manifesto II is neutral on economic system.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Small commune-based society is not a humanist programme, which looks to democratic institutions and world community.

majority-settlement.rationale: Manifesto II opposes discrimination by ethnicity.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Manifesto II criticises both purely capitalist and communist dogma and judges systems by well-being.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Manifesto II calls for a world community and international cooperation, the opposite of autarkic blocs.

assisted-dying.rationale: Manifesto II affirms the right to die with dignity, euthanasia and the right to suicide.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Manifesto II opposes prohibiting sexual behaviour between consenting adults by law or social sanction, though it does not name homosexuality.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Manifesto II supports the legal right of opposition to governmental policies and a full range of civil liberties, and warns against state ideology used to oppress dissenters.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Manifesto II lists religious liberty among essential freedoms and calls separation of church and state an imperative; blasphemy itself is not named.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Manifesto II holds that separation of church and state and of ideology and state are imperatives, so legitimacy cannot rest on religious law, and it favours peaceful change.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Manifesto II says participatory democracy must be extended to the economy, school, family, workplace and voluntary associations.

alienated-labor.rationale: Manifesto II criticises economic injustice but prescribes no economic theory, so adherents range from Marxist-leaning humanists to market liberals; no single view is stated.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Secular humanism holds that ethics and authority rest on human reason and democracy, not divine authority, as the Declaration and Manifesto II state.

rich-first.rationale: The movement prescribes no development path and its equality emphasis pulls against acceptance of uneven growth; adherents are split and the sources are silent.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Humanist Manifesto II commits to democracy and equal rights for all, which leaves no place for inherited rule.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: The movement is silent on debt conditionality; Manifesto II backs international cooperation and aid but adherents split on lender terms.

property-franchise.rationale: Manifesto II demands full democratic participation and equal civil rights, which excludes wealth qualifications for voting.

reification.rationale: This Marxist concept is not part of humanist thought; adherents are split between market-friendly and social-democratic views.

racial-franchise.rationale: Manifesto II condemns discrimination on grounds of race and demands full equality and participation.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Humanists defend individual freedom of marriage and oppose religious discrimination, so state limits on interfaith marriage are rejected.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Manifesto II opposes discrimination on grounds of religion, so singling out shops by owners' faith is rejected.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Secular humanists want strict state neutrality on religion and free inquiry, not state-imposed unbelief; Manifesto II opposes coercion in matters of belief.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The movement prescribes no constitutional form for divided societies; its democratic and universalist principles pull in different directions.

rent-control.rationale: The movement prescribes no housing policy, and adherents split between market and interventionist views.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Humanist ethics are consequence-based and not pacifist, so most adherents accept defensive force, though they weigh it carefully.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Manifesto II looks beyond nationalism toward a transnational community, and secular humanism sees nations as human constructs rather than ancient essences.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Adherents are split: science-minded humanists stress biological sex while others accept constructionist accounts; the sources are silent.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: The sources are silent; its equality principle supports inclusive feminism but does not settle the theory of the category 'women'.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Honouring the dead as martyrs and saints is a religious and nationalist cult that a secular, anti-nationalist movement rejects.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Secular humanism rejects supernatural framings and holds that moral questions are settled by reason and evidence, not as a cosmic struggle.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Manifesto II opposes discrimination and demands equal rights for all, so favouring a national majority in economic life is rejected.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The movement prescribes no economic programme, so the question of what counts as socialism is not one it takes a view on.

second-chamber.rationale: Humanists back democracy but prescribe no legislative structure.

municipal-property.rationale: Manifesto II favors a democratic mixed economy and does not call for community ownership of production.

family-wage.rationale: The movement has no wage doctrine beyond meeting basic needs, and adherents differ.

person-over-state.rationale: Manifesto II holds that the dignity and worth of the individual is central and that society should serve persons' freedom.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Secular humanists affirm meaning, creativity and fulfillment but reject the supernatural, so the word spiritual divides adherents.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Manifesto II calls for ending discrimination on grounds of race and opposes nationalism, so organizing politically by race is rejected.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Secular humanism is cosmopolitan and has no position on linguistic nations, and adherents differ.

communal-electorates.rationale: Manifesto II demands strict separation of church and state, which rules out separate religious electorates.

future-generations.rationale: Manifesto II stresses responsibility to the planet and to humanity's future, though it does not use this phrasing.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its value rests on women's distinct roles, giving their values more weight, a claim about innate nature or no stated position, and the statement now asks only whether women tend to be more compassionate than men.

reviewHistory.rationale: Manifesto II demands equality of the sexes but not a distinct values view; adherents are split.

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its value rests on women's distinct roles, giving their values more weight, a claim about innate nature or no stated position, and the statement now asks only whether women tend to be more compassionate than men.

arms-reduction.rationale: Manifesto II calls for reduction of armaments and for world disarmament and peaceful cooperation.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Manifesto II backs international cooperation and a world community; open treaties are an inference.

capital-controls.rationale: Manifesto II backs a world order and market-friendly civil liberties, with no stated view on capital controls; adherents are split.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Manifesto II calls for narrowing the gap between rich and poor nations and for world economic cooperation.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Its commitment to democracy, civil liberties and reform excludes revolutionary destruction of the state.

sacred-nation.rationale: Manifesto II looks toward world community and rejects the sacralising of any group or nation.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Humanism grounds dignity and rights in a common human nature, though it also embraces human self-improvement.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Secular humanism rests ethics on reason rather than revelation and treats religious claims of ultimate truth as unproven, so it rejects the idea that all religions share one true core.

workers-own-party.rationale: Manifesto II backs workers' rights and social provision but prescribes no party structure.

ban-fgm.rationale: Manifesto II defends human rights and bodily autonomy and condemns practices that subordinate women, so a legal ban follows from its principles.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Manifesto II calls for full equality of the sexes and opposes discrimination, which includes equal property and inheritance rights.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Manifesto II values environmental protection and civil liberties together, so adherents are divided when they clash.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Strict separation of church and state is a core demand, which rules out legal precedence for any one religious interpretation.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Humanists champion democracy tied to human rights, so many would not accept a purely procedural test; the sources do not define it that narrowly.

premarital-sex.rationale: Manifesto II backs sexual freedom between consenting adults and rejects traditional sexual prohibitions.

negative-income-tax.rationale: No economic programme is prescribed; Manifesto II supports social provision but names no mechanism.

women-suffrage.rationale: Manifesto II demands equal rights and opportunity for women and rejects discrimination by sex.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Manifesto II calls for world community and world law, and humanists oppose nationalism, so leaders answer before international courts.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: The Declaration and Manifesto II reject revealed, inerrant scripture and hold that reason and evidence govern belief.

indirect-election.rationale: Humanists stress democracy and civil liberties, which favour direct popular choice of officials.

national-church-status.rationale: Separation of church and state is a core secular humanist position, and privilege for any church is rejected.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Humanists favour minority rights and oppose nationalism, but prescribe no territorial arrangements; split.

simple-living.rationale: Manifesto II backs sustainable use of resources but also affirms enjoyment and abundance; no stance on self-sufficiency, so split.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Manifesto II's defence of civil liberties and due process rules out killing without trial.

close-ties-china.rationale: Manifesto II backs international cooperation without favouring any particular power bloc.

self-ownership.rationale: Manifesto II defends individual freedom over the body, including birth control, abortion and euthanasia.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Its commitment to democracy and pluralism opposes leader-centred politics that bypasses parties and groups.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Strict separation of church and state is the movement's defining political demand, which excludes denominational politics.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Manifesto II says the right to birth control, abortion and divorce should be recognised, with equal rights for women.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: The movement prescribes no economic programme, and adherents are split on financial taxation.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Humanists reject divine or natural-law grounds for authority but also defend conscience and civil liberties; adherents are split.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Manifesto II backs social provision of basic needs and a guaranteed minimum income, so cutting welfare runs against its stated economic ethic. (Carried over from cut-welfare, "Welfare programs create dependency and should be cut.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

missingStatements.text: Medical professionals should be allowed to help terminally ill adults end their lives.
missingStatements.rationale: Manifesto II affirms the right to die with dignity, euthanasia and the right to suicide.

missingStatements.text: Scientific research should not be restricted by religious or moral doctrine.
missingStatements.rationale: Manifesto II opposes censoring research and the Declaration puts free inquiry first, rejecting dogma as authority.

missingStatements.text: Morality can be grounded in human reason and experience without belief in a god.
missingStatements.rationale: Secular humanists hold that ethics needs no supernatural basis.

notes: The text of A Secular Humanist Declaration was not opened (the official site blocked access); only Wikipedia's account of it was. Humanist political views range from libertarian to socialist, which is why economic answers are mostly low-confidence or neutral.
